Data: [TidyTuesday 2026-06-30](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/tree/main/data/2026/2026-06-30).

Ship-wreck icon by [Delapouite](https://game-icons.net), [CC BY 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/).

Of 17,981 recorded Irish shipwrecks, only one in five has ever been given coordinates, and that found share climbs steadily with time: from almost none before 1840, through the World War One turning point, to nearly all after 1950.
The older losses, led by the famine-era 1850s, sink unlocated into the deep, though the pattern also reflects steel hulls and modern sonar, not recency alone.
